Louisville Cardinals.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide directly. The guide records Jeff Brohm winning 10, 9 and 9 games since returning to Louisville in 2023.
Louisville Cardinals.dc: Mark Ivey, the linebackers coach and a Scott Satterfield holdover, and defensive backs coach Steve Ellis, both promoted internally after co-coordinators Ron English and Mark Hagen left.
Louisville Cardinals.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Louisville Cardinals.dc_status: New — the guide records both co-coordinators departing, English stepping away for his son's senior season at Navy, with Brohm promoting from within, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Louisville Cardinals.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Louisville Cardinals.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide's characterisation is that Brohm always makes the passing game work, and that this could be his first 200-yards-per-game rushing attack.
Louisville Cardinals.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Louisville allowing just over 21 points per game in two of three seasons and just over 24 in the other, never allowing more than 3.7 yards per carry under Brohm, and giving up 4.7 yards per play last year, 15th nationally.
Louisville Cardinals.run_pass: Addressed as a possible shift — the guide says this could be Brohm's first 200-yards-per-game rushing attack, with Lincoln Kienholz's running plus the two Browns offsetting an entirely new receiver corps.
Louisville Cardinals.qb_development: Addressed as repeated portal recruitment rather than development. The guide records Miller Moss posting pedestrian numbers after taking over from Tyler Shough, notes both at least arrived with substantial college experience, and records Brohm going to the portal again for Ohio State's Lincoln Kienholz, who threw only 36 passes in three seasons at Columbus.
Louisville Cardinals.continuity: Head coach and offensive coordinator return; the defensive coordinators and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 0 and 0, plus 3 for 14 returning starters, totalling 10.
Louisville Cardinals.staff_turnover: Confined to the defensive side and handled internally. Co-coordinators Ron English and Mark Hagen are gone, and Brohm promoted linebackers coach Mark Ivey and defensive backs coach Steve Ellis.
Louisville Cardinals.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff beyond Ivey being a Scott Satterfield holdover at Louisville. On the roster the guide records Lincoln Kienholz from Ohio State and Davin Wydner from West Georgia.
Louisville Cardinals.portal_recruiting: Repeated at quarterback, and the guide treats getting the position right as a huge start.
Louisville Cardinals.vsin_assessment: Consistent results, one specific recurring flaw. The guide records Brohm winning 10, 9 and 9 games since 2023 while reaching the ACC title game only once, and identifies the flaw precisely: he has lost as a touchdown-or-better favorite at least twice in each of the last three seasons — to Pitt, Kentucky, Stanford, Virginia and Cal — while fairly noting one 2024 loss was to SMU, who became a surprise playoff team. It separately argues that habit has obscured a stellar defense.
Louisville Cardinals.strengths: Three straight nine-win-or-better seasons, offensive-coordinator continuity, a head coach the guide says always makes the passing game work, a defense that has never allowed more than 3.7 yards per carry under him, internal promotions preserving scheme knowledge, and two productive backs.
Louisville Cardinals.concerns: Losing both defensive co-coordinators at once with only one of the top six tacklers back, a quarterback with 36 career passes, and the loss of two receivers who accounted for 132 of the team's 268 receptions and over 54% of its receiving yards.
Louisville Cardinals.betting: The guide ties its recommendation directly to the coaching flaw it identified: cutting the trademark losses as a big favorite from two to one gets this home at a nice plus-money price, even though its own projection is 8.02 wins.

Miami Hurricanes.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Miami Hurricanes.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Miami Hurricanes.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide asks whether Dawson's offense has another gear with a more talented quarterback and notes he impressed in the playoff.
Miami Hurricanes.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Miami Hurricanes.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Miami Hurricanes.qb_development: Addressed through the incoming player's history rather than the staff's record: the guide says Darian Mensah, who had a 34-to-6 ratio at Duke after a strong Tulane season, has been extremely well coached throughout.
Miami Hurricanes.continuity: Head coach and both coordinators return; the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 12.
Miami Hurricanes.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning, and the guide calls both outstanding last season.
Miami Hurricanes.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Darian Mensah arriving from Duke by way of Tulane, and his Duke teammate Cooper Barkate following him.
Miami Hurricanes.portal_recruiting: The guide leans on the programme's recruiting pipeline, especially defensively, as its reason for expecting the defensive losses to be absorbed.
Miami Hurricanes.vsin_assessment: Two readings held together and deliberately unresolved. The guide says much-maligned Mario Cristobal exterminated some demons while noting those demons were present in the regular season with two losses as a double-digit favorite. Its answer to how to evaluate the season is that a lot went right at once — Carson Beck excellent, the defense ferocious, both coordinators outstanding — then supplies the counter-pattern of earlier losses to Georgia Tech and Syracuse as a big favorite, characterises 2025 as a month-long perfect storm arriving at the right time, and leaves the question open: which Miami is the real one?
Miami Hurricanes.strengths: Both coordinators returning after seasons the guide calls outstanding, a quarterback upgrade the guide describes as objectively more talented and extremely well coached, the whole backfield back, a 1,200-yard receiver leading a rebuilt group, and a recruiting pipeline the guide expects to cover defensive losses.
Miami Hurricanes.concerns: A documented pattern of losses as a heavy favorite, 22 combined sacks to replace from two departed linemen, a second-leading tackler and interception leader drafted, another defensive back gone in the fourth round, and a coordinator who must find new go-to players quickly.
Miami Hurricanes.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument, though its favorite-losses pattern is stated in market terms.

NC State Wolfpack.oc: Kurt Roper, in his second year.
NC State Wolfpack.dc: DJ Eliot, in his second year.
NC State Wolfpack.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
NC State Wolfpack.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
NC State Wolfpack.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
NC State Wolfpack.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide describes the receiving picture as genuinely distributed rather than empty — nobody exceeded 629 yards, but four players had 430 or more and seven had at least 37 catches — and hopes for standouts rather than a repeat of the committee approach.
NC State Wolfpack.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 20 sacks, tied for 107th; nine interceptions; 128th in third-down defense; and over 200 plays of 10-plus yards allowed.
NC State Wolfpack.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
NC State Wolfpack.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records CJ Bailey producing 31 total touchdowns with over 3,100 passing yards and 215 rushing, and returning.
NC State Wolfpack.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 43) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 2 for 10 returning starters — totalling 16.
NC State Wolfpack.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning in their second year.
NC State Wolfpack.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Tad Hudson from Coastal Carolina, Victor Snow from Buffalo and Joshisa Trader from Miami.
NC State Wolfpack.portal_recruiting: Addressed as volume rather than as a staff strategy — the guide notes the second-year coordinators have a lot of work to do with many younger players and a large number of transfers.
NC State Wolfpack.vsin_assessment: Longevity framed against the modern game, and a ceiling question asked honestly. The guide frames Doeren's 14th season against a landscape where long-tenured coaches are retiring or struggling to keep up with the modern offseason. On the ceiling it records a slightly above average offense, a roughly average defense and a team lacking explosiveness, then widens the sample honestly — only 2021 was statistically special at +11.4 points and +1.2 yards per play, and that team still went only 9-4.
NC State Wolfpack.strengths: A Stability Score of 16 with head coach, both coordinators and the quarterback all returning; a quarterback with 31 total touchdowns; a red-zone touchdown percentage ranked second nationally; and a receiving group with genuine depth if not a standout.
NC State Wolfpack.concerns: The loss of the top five receivers and the leading rusher, and on defense the leading tackler, the two next-highest sack producers, the sack leader, the top pass rusher and the pass-breakup leader — leaving second-year coordinators with a lot of work, many younger players and a large number of transfers.
NC State Wolfpack.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

North Carolina Tar Heels.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide in college terms. The guide's characterisation is that Bill Belichick is a defensive genius, and it records year one of the experiment.
North Carolina Tar Heels.oc: Bobby Petrino, hired after Freddie Kitchens was dismissed.
North Carolina Tar Heels.dc: Not addressed in guide. Belichick himself is credited with the defensive improvement.
North Carolina Tar Heels.oc_status: New — the guide records Kitchens' dismissal and Petrino's hire, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
North Carolina Tar Heels.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
North Carolina Tar Heels.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
North Carolina Tar Heels.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
North Carolina Tar Heels.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records North Carolina having its best defense in some time, allowing 4.9 yards per play, 3.5 yards per carry and 24.5 points per game, including 25 against conference opponents.
North Carolina Tar Heels.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records the team averaging 3.7 yards per carry.
North Carolina Tar Heels.qb_development: Not addressed as a record, but the guide states an explicit preference among the candidates: it likes North Carolina more if Miles O'Neill — a Petrino recruit at Texas A&M — or four-star freshman Travis Burgess start over Billy Edwards, and argues the programme should bet on upside rather than on a mediocre Maryland starter from two seasons ago.
North Carolina Tar Heels.continuity: Head coach and defensive coordinator return; the offensive coordinator and quarterback change. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 0, 3 and 0, plus 1 for 9 returning starters, totalling 8.
North Carolina Tar Heels.staff_turnover: Confined to the offensive side, where Freddie Kitchens was dismissed and Bobby Petrino hired.
North Carolina Tar Heels.prior_school: Texas A&M is the connection the guide draws for the quarterback room, noting Miles O'Neill is a Petrino recruit. It records Billy Edwards' route as Wake Forest, Maryland, Wisconsin and now North Carolina.
North Carolina Tar Heels.portal_recruiting: Treated as the clearest evidence the staff is working. Despite a mass exodus to the portal, North Carolina kept its leading rusher, leading receiver and leading sack man, which the guide reads as Belichick and former VSiN personality Michael Lombardi identifying who to pay to stay and who to pay to come. It also records North Carolina signing the 19th-ranked recruiting class with over 40 recruits, with only West Virginia taking more 2026 commitments — so whatever the school is selling, players are buying. On the quarterback it reports Wisconsin was said to have paid around $1 million in NIL compensation for Edwards and suggests North Carolina may have got a deal.
North Carolina Tar Heels.vsin_assessment: A failed-looking year one with a substantial and specific counterweight. The guide's overall verdict is that year one looked like a failure, with the PR department busy over Belichick's much younger girlfriend and messy play on the field, and the offense putrid enough to cost bowl eligibility for the first time since 2018. Against that it credits a defensive genius and the programme's best defense in some time, records the recruiting haul, and says a case can be made for real hope this season with a sense that Belichick is closer to making this work.
North Carolina Tar Heels.strengths: A head coach the guide calls a defensive genius, coming off the programme's best defense in some time; retention of the leading rusher, receiver and sack man against a mass portal exodus; the 19th-ranked recruiting class with over 40 recruits; and a new offensive coordinator with a recruit of his own already in the quarterback room.
North Carolina Tar Heels.concerns: An offense the guide calls putrid, a quarterback room whose presumed starter it argues against, poor external optics from the hiring and off-field matters, and only nine returning starters.
North Carolina Tar Heels.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though the guide states a coaching-adjacent preference: it likes North Carolina more if O'Neill or Burgess start over Edwards.

Pittsburgh Panthers.previous_hc_experience: Not addressed in guide. The guide records Pat Narduzzi in his 12th season and refers to his defensive record.
Pittsburgh Panthers.oc: Kade Bell, entering year three of his offense.
Pittsburgh Panthers.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the guide refers to year three of the Kade Bell offense.
Pittsburgh Panthers.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Pittsburgh Panthers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Pittsburgh Panthers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme beyond being called the Kade Bell offense, now in year three.
Pittsburgh Panthers.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's reference point is Narduzzi's defensive record.
Pittsburgh Panthers.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide records Pitt averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, 119th nationally.
Pittsburgh Panthers.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Mason Heintschel having the job outright because Eli Holstein is at Virginia, and being solid as a true freshman across nine starts.
Pittsburgh Panthers.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes, as does the special teams coordinator. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 3 for 13 returning starters, totalling 14.
Pittsburgh Panthers.staff_turnover: The guide singles out a special-teams change as consequential: coordinator Jacob Bronowski left for Auburn, replaced by Mike Priefer, who was fired from the same role at North Carolina. It calls special teams an underrated facet that helped Pitt a lot last season and may not this time, with a new kicker, a new punter and new returners as well.
Pittsburgh Panthers.prior_school: Auburn is where Bronowski went; North Carolina is where Priefer was fired from the same role. On the roster the guide records Netinho Olivieri from Penn and Sam Hunsaker from Northern Arizona.
Pittsburgh Panthers.portal_recruiting: Addressed at specific positions — new blind-side protection from Penn transfer Netinho Olivieri, and a kicker from Northern Arizona whose numbers the guide discounts for altitude.
Pittsburgh Panthers.vsin_assessment: Sceptical of the surface numbers, candid about not resolving them. The guide characterises 2025 as a roller coaster and dismantles the scoring: 20th in points per game while ranking 67th in yards per play and 120th in third-down conversion rate, allowing 44 sacks — fifth-most nationally. It locates the points in four pick-sixes among 15 interceptions, punt return touchdowns and four kick returns of 40-plus yards, shows the pattern is not new, and concludes unusually candidly that it does not know what to make of it but that special teams prowess has a lot to do with it. It also pushes back directly on other previews talking up the offensive line's experience, observing the experience in question is in letting defenders reach the quarterback — 87 sacks allowed over two seasons.
Pittsburgh Panthers.strengths: A head coach with a defensive record the guide treats as a reason to see playoff potential on a friendly schedule, a settled quarterback in year two, offensive-coordinator continuity entering year three of the system, and 13 returning starters.
Pittsburgh Panthers.concerns: A new defensive coordinator, a special-teams unit rebuilt around a coordinator fired from the same role elsewhere plus a new kicker, punter and returners — after special teams supplied much of last year's scoring — and an offensive line that has allowed 87 sacks over two seasons with many of the same contributors back.
Pittsburgh Panthers.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-adjacent market caution is that last season's point total should be viewed sceptically.

SMU Mustangs.oc: Rhett Lashlee calls his own plays. The guide records that he lost right-hand man Casey Woods to the Missouri State head job, and notes wryly that D'Eriq King is now a co-coordinator.
SMU Mustangs.dc: Maurice Crum, new, alongside holdover co-coordinator Ricky Hunley Jr, promoted from within after Scott Symons left for the Dallas Cowboys.
SMU Mustangs.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator, and the head coach calls the plays himself.
SMU Mustangs.dc_status: New — the guide records Scott Symons leaving for the Cowboys, Lashlee promoting from within, and Maurice Crum taking over with Ricky Hunley Jr as co-coordinator; the Stability Score table (p. 44) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
SMU Mustangs.offensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records SMU exceeding six yards per play on offense in all four Lashlee seasons.
SMU Mustangs.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records 125 sacks over three seasons and a +9 turnover margin with 28 takeaways last year.
SMU Mustangs.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split. The guide identifies the biggest year-over-year change as Kevin Jennings doing virtually nothing as a runner after 300 more rushing yards in 2024.
SMU Mustangs.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide records Jennings posting a 26-to-13 touchdown-to-interception ratio with double-digit interceptions in each of the last two seasons, while crediting him with managing sacks well — only 33 taken on well over 800 dropbacks — and with 171 carries over two seasons that turned potential negatives into neutral or slightly positive plays.
SMU Mustangs.continuity: Head coach, offensive coordinator and quarterback return; the defensive coordinator changes. The Stability Score table (p. 44) prints 4, 3, 0 and 4, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 13.
SMU Mustangs.staff_turnover: Two departures the guide records: Casey Woods, Lashlee's right-hand man, left for the Missouri State head job, and former defensive coordinator Scott Symons is still in Dallas but with the Cowboys. Both replacements were internal promotions.
SMU Mustangs.prior_school: Not addressed in guide for the staff. On the roster the guide records Kendrick Raphael arriving at his third ACC school.
SMU Mustangs.portal_recruiting: Flagged as a weakness relative to need. Per 247Sports, SMU brought in only the sixth-ranked portal class among 17 ACC teams, with many needs at impact positions.
SMU Mustangs.vsin_assessment: Success framed as a retention risk. The guide opens by asking whether this is Lashlee's last season in Dallas, records 11-win seasons in 2023 and 2024 and another successful 2025 at 38-16, and expects suitors to come calling and tough decisions to follow with Kevin Jennings out of eligibility after this season. It argues defense has been the separator between his 7-6 debut and 31-10 over three years, and introduces sack differential as a metric some handicappers it respects treat as a major tenet — SMU was +16 last season, down from +25 and +31 in the two prior years.
SMU Mustangs.strengths: A head coach who is 38-16 and calls his own plays, offensive production above six yards per play in all four of his seasons, 125 sacks over three seasons, a returning quarterback the guide credits with unusual sack avoidance, and internal promotions on both vacated jobs.
SMU Mustangs.concerns: A head coach the guide expects to attract suitors, the loss of his right-hand man on offense and his defensive coordinator, five of the top seven tacklers gone including the sack leader with all four Mustangs who had at least five sacks departed, the loss of four of the top five receivers and both leading rushers, and only the sixth-ranked portal class in the conference against many needs.
SMU Mustangs.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit market recommendation tied to coaching, though the guide frames sack differential — a coaching-linked metric it says respected handicappers treat as a major tenet — as trending the wrong way.
